digest.en: Tajikistan is raising the world's tallest dam while Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case. Kenya is deploying Big Tech for state control as Ukraine rescues a soldier by drone.
digest.hi: रुबियो की क्वाड लौटने की घोषणा और पुतिन के युद्ध वार्ता के लिए तैयार होने की खबरें आज की प्रमुख घटनाएं हैं। इसी बीच, ट्रंप से जुड़े डेटा लीक केस में अदालत ने 25 बिलियन डॉलर का जुर्माना लगाया है।

articles.title: 'World's Tallest' Dam Takes Shape In Tajikistan
articles.summary: Tajikistan is advancing the Soviet-era Roghun Dam project after securing major funding tranches. The development aims to reshape Central Asia's energy supply. The construction will displace tens of thousands of local villagers from their homes. The Soviet-era Roghun Dam project has endured decades of uncertainty and opposition. Now major funding tranches appear to have the project on track to transform Central Asia's energy landscape -- and displace tens of thousands of Tajik villagers.

articles.title: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
articles.summary: New Taipei prosecutors charged five men with plotting to injure comedian Huang Yi-hao. A Chinese national allegedly paid them to ram a car into him. Huang had mocked Xi Jinping and the Chinese Communist party. Person named ‘K’ from China paid five defendants to injure Huang Yi-hao, New Taipei prosecutors sayTaiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping. Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has.

articles.title: When Big Tech becomes a tool of state control in Kenya
articles.summary: Access Now reported 313 global internet shutdowns in 2025. Africa saw 30 outages across 15 countries. Protests triggered most cuts. Elections followed as the second leading cause for these digital blackouts. Access Now's 2025 report found that at least 313 shutdowns were implemented globally, and that in Africa the Internet was shut down 30 times in 15 countries, with protests the leading trigger, followed by elections.

articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
articles.summary: Families report ICE is deporting severely ill detainees from Florida jails. Flights to unknown African countries are scheduled for Wednesday. Advocates say the detainees have no ties to these destinations despite worsening medical conditions. Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detailRelatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions. Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocac.

articles.title: Migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees on European sea routes
articles.summary: The UN reported that migrants paid up to 500 million dollars in smuggling fees on European sea routes last year. The figures come from a joint report by UNODC and the International Organization for Migration. The price tag for smuggling on European sea routes reached up to half a billion dollars last year, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the UN migration office, IOM, reported on Wednesday.

articles.title: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
articles.summary: Sudan peace talks resumed in Geneva on Wednesday. Nearly two dozen countries met to discuss a ceasefire. The goal is a transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people amid the ongoing drone war. Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.

articles.title: Global warming will breach 1.5°C – but deep, fast cuts can still bring it back
articles.summary: Global temperatures will exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Nations must implement deep, rapid emissions cuts to minimize this overshoot. The goal is returning to the agreed threshold by century's end. Urgent action is required to limit the duration of this breach. With global temperature rise set to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, countries “must pull out all the stops” and urgently cut emissions to minimize the overshoot and return to the internationally agreed threshold by the end of this century.

articles.title: Shark trapped for a month in South Korean canal is finally freed
articles.summary: A shark named Bukang-i was freed from a South Korean canal after being trapped for a month. The animal attracted 1.6 million visitors during its confinement. Local volunteers monitored its condition daily. Bukang-i successfully guided out after month in which it drew 1.6m visitors and was watched over by YouTubersIn South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch.

articles.title: US Citizen Accused By Moscow Of Fighting For Ukraine Released From Russian Prison
articles.summary: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired Michigan teacher, was released from Russian custody. He had been detained since 2022 on charges of joining Ukraine's armed forces. The Kremlin framed his release as a goodwill gesture. His freedom marks a significant shift in the ongoing diplomatic standoff. Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan held by Russia since 2022 on accusations of joining Ukraine's armed forces, has been freed in what is being framed as a goodwill gesture by the Kremlin.

articles.title: Vladimir Putin’s Neighbors: Two Parallel Worlds On Lake Valdai
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin's residence near Lake Valdai features heavy security and air defenses. Locals nearby face restricted access to the lake and forests. Families in the region bear the economic costs of Russia's war against Ukraine. The area exists as two parallel worlds of privilege and restriction. Vladimir Putin’s secluded residence near Russia’s Lake Valdai is surrounded by fences, security forces, and air defenses.

articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.summary: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in Abuja. A woman who traveled from Uganda tested positive after showing symptoms on 7 October. The diagnosis marks the outbreak's spread into West Africa's most populous nation. Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from UgandaNigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said. The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola.

articles.title: Wounded Ukrainian Soldier Rescued From Front Lines By Aerial Drone
articles.summary: Ukraine's military rescued a wounded soldier from the front lines using an aerial drone. The soldier, injured in both legs, strapped himself to a hexacopter for evacuation. Fellow servicemen described the act as heroic. This marks the first recorded instance of such a drone-based battlefield rescue. In what Ukraine's military is calling a historic first, a soldier who suffered injuries to both legs on the battlefield was evacuated by an unmanned aerial drone.

articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
articles.summary: Alberta voters rejected a proposal to begin the independence process by a wide margin. Nearly 1.9 million votes were counted, with 76 percent supporting remaining in Canada. The result delivered a decisive victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity. Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unityVoters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement. articles.title: Ukraine Liberates Dnipropetrovsk Settlements, But Villages Lie In Ruins
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces retaken 26 settlements in the Dnipropetrovsk region. The villages are largely destroyed and uninhabitable. Russian troops are being pushed back, but Ukrainian forces face challenges holding the reclaimed territory under constant drone threat. As Russian troops are pushed back, Ukrainian forces face the challenge of holding the reclaimed territory under constant threat from drones. Ukraine Liberates Dnipropetrovsk Settlements, But Villages Lie In Ruins.

articles.title: With War In Limbo, Influential Iranian Officials Openly Call For A Nuclear Bomb
articles.summary: Influential Iranian officials are openly calling for a nuclear bomb. The death of Ali Khamenei has weakened the political taboo surrounding the weapon. Debate is growing over whether the Islamic republic should abandon its long-standing position against developing nukes. Ali Khamenei's death may not have invalidated his nuclear fatwa, but it has weakened the political taboo surrounding the bomb. Debate is now growing over whether the Islamic republic should abandon its long-standing position against developing nukes.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro’s debate comment calling his rival corrupt backfired. Social media users quickly turned the moment into a viral meme. The stunt was meant to highlight alleged crookedness before the election runoff. Instead, it became a widespread parody online. Far-right presidential candidate’s TV debate swipe at rival backfires as people take to social media to parody itTo Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election. But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Lu.

articles.title: Georgia Faces New Test As Court Weighs Ban On 5 Opposition Parties
articles.summary: Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearings on October 21 regarding a ban on five opposition parties. These parties have collectively won hundreds of thousands of votes. The proceedings mark another critical test for the country’s multiparty democracy, with a final ruling potentially to come later. Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearings on October 21 on a case seeking to ban five opposition parties that together have won hundreds of thousands of votes.

articles.title: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
articles.summary: Over 250,000 people have fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the United Nations reported. Access to the southwestern city of Taiz is essentially blocked. This has trapped residents in areas facing severe hunger and disease. The displacement continues to strain local humanitarian resources. More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said on Tuesday, citing particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is “essentially blocked”.

articles.title: Moldova To Probe Possible Russian Data-Harvesting After RFE/RL Investigation
articles.summary: Moldova launched an investigation into Yandex for allegedly harvesting citizen data. The company reportedly sent personal information to Russian servers instead of the Netherlands. This contradicts previous data storage agreements. The probe follows an investigation by Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. Moldova has announced an investigation into concerns that Russian tech giant Yandex has been harvesting the personal data of its citizens by sending it directly to servers in Russia rather than storing it in the Netherlands as previously believed.

articles.title: Why Starshield’s slowdown really hurts Ukraine
articles.summary: SpaceX temporarily restricted Starshield satellite internet for Ukrainian forces. This slowdown has raised serious concerns in Kyiv and among its allies. The military-grade service supports critical battlefield communications. The disruption highlights Ukraine’s dependence on external satellite infrastructure. Reports that SpaceX temporarily restricted its satellite internet service for Ukraine’s armed forces have generated serious concern in Kyiv and among the country’s allies.

articles.title: After Oslo Talks, Zelenskyy Thanks US As Missile Intelligence 'Works Now'
articles.summary: Zelenskyy thanked the United States after Oslo talks. He said missile intelligence now works effectively. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner joined the meetings. Russia continues to bomb Ukraine while tensions between Kyiv and Washington grow. US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will take part in meetings in Oslo to discuss the situation in Ukraine with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Russia continues to pound the country amid growing tensions between Kyiv and Washington.

articles.title: Dhaka’s silence on Saudi executions puts remittances over lives
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshis on October 14, prompting minimal diplomatic reaction from Dhaka. The foreign ministry requested details but assured Riyadh that bilateral relations would remain unaffected. This restrained official response contrasts sharply with widespread public anger on social media, highlighting a preference for remittance stability over immediate political protest. Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshis on October 14 but Dhaka’s response was conspicuously restrained.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
articles.summary: Hurricane Trudy weakened to a tropical storm after threatening Mexico's Pacific coast. The system remained 160 kilometers southwest of the shore. Meanwhile, deadly floods in Greece killed one person. The Pacific season saw 22 named systems this year. Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in GreeceIn contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system.

articles.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
articles.summary: China's third-quarter GDP grew by 4.5 percent year-on-year. The figure exceeded previous forecasts. Strong electronics demand boosted industrial output and exports. Factory growth significantly outpaced consumer spending during the July to September period. Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demandBusiness live – latest updatesRoaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending. China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on.

articles.title: Three deaths from float crushes raise safety concerns over Japanese festivals
articles.summary: Three people died from float crushes at Japanese festivals this weekend. Deputy mayor Akihiro Nabae was killed in Saijo. Two other men died in similar incidents elsewhere in the country. Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhereThere is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country. articles.summary: मार्को रूबियो ने कहा कि क्वाड शिखर सम्मेलन 2026 के अंत से पहले मनीला में होगा। उन्होंने भारत-अमेरिका व्यापार समझौते के कुछ हफ्तों में पूरा होने की उम्मीद जताई। अमेरिकी विदेश मंत्री मार्को रूबियो ने नेटवर्क18 के एडिटर-इन-चीफ राहुल जोशी को दिए एक्सक्लूसिव इंटरव्यू में भारत-अमेरिका संबंधों को लेकर कई अहम संकेत दिए. उन्होंने उम्मीद जताई कि क्वाड नेताओं की बैठक 2026 के अंत से पहले मनीला में होगी और दोनों देशों की ट्रेड डील कुछ हफ्तों में पूरी हो सकती है.

articles.title: ट्रंप के दबाव का असर? युद्ध पर बातचीत को तैयार हुए पुतिन, रूस-यूक्रेन-अमेरिका कब से करेंगे बात?
articles.summary: पुतिन ने यूक्रेन युद्ध समाधान के लिए अमेरिका और यूक्रेन के साथ त्रिपक्षीय वार्ता शुरू करने पर सहमति दी। बातचीत 10 नवंबर के बाद शुरू हो सकती है। रूसी राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन ने यूक्रेन युद्ध खत्म करने के लिए अमेरिका और यूक्रेन के साथ त्रिपक्षीय वार्ता फिर शुरू करने पर सैद्धांतिक सहमति दी है. सेंट पीटर्सबर्ग में पुतिन और अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप के दूत स्टीव विटकॉफ के बीच करीब तीन घंटे बैठक हुई.

articles.summary: मालदीव और पाकिस्तान ने रक्षा, समुद्री सुरक्षा और व्यापार सहित 20 समझौतों पर हस्ताक्षर किए। दोनों देशों ने दो वर्षों में व्यापार को 200 मिलियन डॉलर तक पहुंचाने का लक्ष्य रखा है। मालदीव के राष्ट्रपति मोहम्मद मुइज्जू के पाकिस्तान दौरे के दौरान दोनों देशों ने रक्षा सहयोग, समुद्री सुरक्षा, साइबर सुरक्षा और व्यापार सहित 20 समझौतों पर हस्ताक्षर किए. दोनों देशों ने अगले दो साल में व्यापार को 200 मिलियन डॉलर तक पहुंचाने का लक्ष्य रखा है.

articles.title: किम जोंग उन की बहन ने सीमा पर संभाला मोर्चा, दक्षिण कोरिया को दी चेतावनी
articles.summary: किम यो जोंग ने दक्षिण कोरियाई सीमा पर सैन्य किलेबंदी का निरीक्षण किया। उन्होंने दक्षिण कोरिया को किसी भी उकसावे पर कड़ी जवाबी कार्रवाई की चेतावनी दी। सीमा पर तनाव बढ़ रहा है। नई दिल्ली। उत्तर कोरिया और दक्षिण कोरिया के बीच तनाव एक बार फिर बढ़ता नजर आ रहा है। उत्तर कोरियाई नेता किम जोंग उन की बहन किम यो जोंग ने दक्षिण कोरिया से लगी सीमा के अग्रिम क्षेत्रों का दौरा कर वहां चल रहे सैन्य किलेबंदी के कार्यों का निरीक्षण किया।

articles.title: अमेरिकी संसद उम्मीदवार सहित 70 से ज्यादा लोगों को इजराइली फौज ने पकड़ा, क्या है पूरा मामला?
articles.summary: इजराइली सेना ने वेस्ट बैंक में जैतून की फसल काटने वाले 70 से अधिक लोगों को पकड़ा। इनमें अमेरिकी संसद के एक उम्मीदवार भी शामिल थे। सुरक्षा बलों ने उन्हें घेर लिया। इजराइली सुरक्षा बलों ने अमेरकी संसद चुनाव के उम्मीदवार सहित 70 से ज्यादा लोगों को पकड़ लिया है। इजराइली फौज ने वेस्ट बैंक के एक गांव में जैतून की फसल काटने के दौरान इन लोगों को घेर लिया।
